text: decision_log_entry is P7's, so RWB-P1-DM012-APP reads the legacy entries once at cutover, records each one as a local decision record plus its outbox row in rwb_source_data through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, and publishes DecisionRecorded on rwb.decision-record.v1 for rwb-decision to seal into the central ledger; nothing is handed over as a file and no decision_log_entry row is written by P1.
why: One schema and one login per service and no cross-schema write, so a P1 story cannot insert into P7's ledger table, while the open-case set, the ACE keys and the reconciliation are P1's and cannot be read by P7 without a contract hop.
read: Ownership Map v1 (decision_log_entry owner P7); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-03 and R4 (rwb.decision-record.v1); TSD P1 v3 T1.1 boundary rule and T6.3 grants; legacy RWB-DM-012 AC1.
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-decision technical owner at the wave-4 contract review
impact: AC1 keeps the legacy wording and adds the rwb-decision contract fake as its first Given; no C dependency is recorded because the ledger is read through a fake and the seal is the owner's own consumer.

text: Every migrated entry keeps its own chain_seq, prev_hash and entry_hash, and the first decision record written in rwb-source-data after cutover takes the entry_hash of the last migrated entry as its prev_hash; no entry is renumbered or re-hashed, and the 02:00 chain check (JOB-14) stays with rwb-decision.
why: AC1 forbids rewriting, renumbering or re-hashing and calls the log append-only, but no source states how a chain in the monolith's single log continues inside a service's own decision records.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-012 AC1; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-03; ADR-022 (local decision record plus central ledger); Ownership Map v1 decision_log_entry (P7).
confirm: Solution architect at the PRD (C1) and the rwb-decision technical owner at the wave-4 contract review
impact: Section 4 fixes the continuation rule in the writer's configuration and in one test; JOB-14 and the chain verification remain P7's and are named out of scope.

text: The cutover evidence is ten consecutive business dates of PASS reconciliation results with no unexplained variance and no new REC-05 orphan on a migrated entry's case, read from reconciliation_result; the sign-off is held in the cutover record of the release pipeline, and the legacy tables stay read-only for the retention class of their record class.
why: AC3 names ten clean days, a sign-off and a retention period but no source gives the measure, the record that holds the sign-off or the length of the period.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-012 AC3; FSD P1 v3 A2.11 (REC-01, REC-02, REC-05) and A2.17 (retention class); TSD P1 v3 T3.6 (reconciliation_result) and T3.8.
confirm: Data steward and data product owner at the cutover sign-off
impact: A break resets the count, no counter table and no sign-off table is created, and the period is confirmed in the cutover plan rather than in code.

text: AC2 Reconcile the business keys, the REC-05 step and its test case TC-DM-012-02 sit with RWB-ITG-DM012-ITG, so RWB-P1-DM012-APP owns AC1 and AC3 only and keeps TC-DM-012-01, TC-DM-012-03, TC-DM-012-04 and TC-DM-012-05.
why: The Work Package assigns AC1 and AC3 to this story, and REC-05 is the daily reconciliation of the service across services rather than a cutover extract step.
read: WP B2-P1-011 story line (acs AC1, AC3); legacy RWB-DM-012 AC2 and test cases; FSD P1 v3 A2.11.3 (REC-05); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-05.
impact: AC2 and TC-DM-012-02 are not restated here; the ITG story owns them as TC-DM-012-02-ITG and no AC or TC is duplicated across the two stories.
